heuristic.applicability: Prefer when blue appears attached and elevated, is already moving toward the destination, or is near the observed blue goal and terminal placement/release accuracy dominates. It is also a useful alternative when an upstream controller hands off later than demonstrated. It remains trained across every assigned action and both overlaps, rather than being a phase-trimmed subpolicy.

handoff.entry_conditions: Red is at/near the central buffer and blue is the intended object; this policy may enter at the normal red-release overlap or later when blue is already elevated or en route to its goal.
handoff.exit_conditions: Blue is visibly stationary inside the observed blue goal, gripper open and TCP retreating; later supervised exit is allowed after buffered red closure and initial lift.
handoff.failure_signatures: Blue not co-moving during carry, descent offset from the goal, opening while high, object still attached after opening, red disturbed, or IK residuals staying high. Use the object-frame prior for a displaced source and the fresh-TCP prior for moderate off-nominal servo state.
handoff.overlap_role: The package retains and action-supervises the full 210-230 step predecessor overlap and 230-240 step successor overlap reported for the demonstrations, including contact-critical approach/close/lift actions.
handoff.successor_readiness: A robust switch cue is settled blue plus an open/clear gripper. If continuation uses the tail, switch after buffered red follows the closed gripper upward. Keep the supplied task success definition unchanged.

heuristic.limitations: Goal anchoring does not make pregrasp approach invariant to a displaced source blue and may be weak when blue is far from the goal; select the blue-object-frame prior there. Quaternion projection can map an extreme off-distribution sample to an unintended rotation, although training labels are tightly clustered. This prior has no contact truth and cannot establish that blue is actually held; select based on observed co-motion and geometry, not gripper command alone. Fresh-TCP increments better cover modest tracking offsets during an otherwise valid phase. No prior here demonstrates recovery from a drop, collision, wrong-object pickup, or unreachable shifted goal.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Use the unchanged DiffusionBackbone and full fixed temporal recipe. encode_targets subtracts the causal chunk blue-goal position from commanded world TCP positions and emits canonical FK quaternion plus gripper. decode_action adds the same goal position, normalizes the sampled quaternion, creates a world pose and uses solve_ik from current joints. The high-level agent should route a held/elevated blue or late entry here; representation normalization is fit on these 8D authorized labels only.
heuristic.rationale: Observed evidence: blue is securely carried around z=0.28-0.30 at demo10100:520-580 and demo10105:510-570, then descends at the blue goal (600-620 and 590-610), is settled near (-0.352,-0.200,0.020) and opened by 640/630, and remains fixed there during retreat and the successor's red pickup. Destination-relative targets expose the demonstrated terminal geometry directly rather than requiring the model to reproduce a narrow world coordinate. Expected benefit is robust placement under an observed goal displacement and under entry after pickup; demonstrations themselves have a fixed goal, so this is a geometric prior, not measured shifted-goal performance.
heuristic.statement: Blue-goal-frame absolute Cartesian targets. Learn the commanded TCP position relative to the observed blue-goal point, together with a canonical world-frame wxyz target quaternion and native gripper scalar (8 dimensions). Goal-centric two-frame inputs include TCP, blue and buffered-red poses relative to the goal, qpos/qvel, goal separation and the blue goal's world position. The actual goal is resolved at each replan and fixed for the sampled chunk. This directly anchors blue lowering, release and retreat to the destination and reduces sensitivity to a changed destination or to entering after blue has already been lifted. Quaternion normalization in decode is the declared projection; the standard backbone is unchanged.

subgoal: Accept the scene while red is finishing its buffer release, retreat from red, approach the blue block in the initially red region, close from above, lift and carry blue to the blue goal near (-0.35,-0.20), lower and release it, then retreat. The core responsibility is blue-to-blue-goal relocation. The tail is extended through approach, grasp, and initial lift of buffered red.
